entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 EETAsia Cognex Wafer Reader Helps IC Manufacturers Scale Production Cognex's In-Sight 1750 wafer and panel identification system helps chip makers reduce disruptions, improve traceability, and maintain throughput. The post Cognex Wafer Reader Helps IC Manufacturers Scale Production appeared first on EE Times Asia . Semiconductor Read
2 EETAsia Singapore Expands Semiconductor Talent Pipeline from Primary Schools to Regional Universities Singapore semiconductor sector expands early education, industry exposure and regional exchanges to develop future technical talent across Asia. The post Singapore Expands Semiconductor Talent Pipeline from Primary Schools to Regional Universities appeared first on EE Times Asia . Semiconductor Read

5 DigiTimes Microsoft to invest US$10B in Middle East AI infrastructure, despite war risks Microsoft announced that it will invest US$10 billion in expanding AI infrastructure in the Middle East by 2030. The commitment directs funding to a region facing threats from the war in Iran, where data center construction has continued despite the ongoing conflict. AI Read
6 DigiTimes Anduril's Taiwan supply chain to grow 15-fold in 2026 US defense tech unicorn Anduril plans to expand its overall investment in Taiwan, with procurement from its Taiwan supply chain expected to grow 15-fold in 2026, founder Palmer Luckey said at the International Forum of the Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee. Logistics Read
7 TechAsia From finishing tasks to driving ROI: A VC product guide Felicis' Peter Deng explains why products must solve real customer problems, and how AI is changing how companies hire and evaluate startups. AI Read
8 DigiTimes Taiwan's homegrown trainer program ends with 66 Brave Eagles delivered AIDC's Brave Eagle advanced jet trainer, a flagship "made-in-Taiwan" defense program, completed development and mass production on September 24, with AIDC chairman Chin-Pin Tsao personally leading the final delivery. The handover means all 66 production aircraft have now been delivered, marking a new chapter for Taiwan Logistics Read
9 TechAsia Mapping the trailblazing startups in Australia’s AI sector Mapping Australia's AI sector: Key players, top investors, and funding insights in one report. AI Read
10 TechAsia Gobi-backed Bitsmedia lays off 21 employees The company's managing director and CEO says AI was "not a factor in the decision" and that it has no plans for further restructuring at this time. AI Read
11 NikkeiAsia Trump-Xi summit live: US, China should keep AI under human control, Xi says Trump-Xi summit live: US, China should keep AI under human control, Xi says AI Read

entry.content:

Semiconductor Read

entry.title: Asia Tech News Digest - September 22, 2026
entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 TechAsia Tencent Cloud, AI Singapore launch hackathon Tencent said outstanding participants may be considered for fast-track internships. AI Read
2 TechAsia Bain Capital leads $25m round for AI health startup Corridor Its founder previously led product at Scale AI and explored chronic pain care. AI Read
3 TechAsia Amazon to invest $1.9b in delivery, expand AI tools Surround-view cameras will reach half of Amazon’s Rivian vans by year-end. AI Read
4 CNA Trump returns to UN at a moment of anxiety about Iran, AI and the future of world body itself US President Donald Trump returns to the General Assembly nearing the seven-month mark of a new war against Iran that he insists is necessary to address a nuclear threat. AI Read
5 DigiTimes Microsoft opens fourth India cloud region, casting Hyderabad as an AI hub for Asia and the Global South Microsoft has turned a headline slice of its US$20.5 billion India commitment into operating infrastructure, opening a Hyderabad cloud region it intends to serve customers well beyond India's borders. The move positions the country as a supply base for AI compute at a moment when it generates far more data than it can AI Read
6 DigiTimes Hanmi Semiconductor ships first FC Bonder 75 for 2.5D packaging Hanmi Semiconductor said on September 22 that it has shipped its first FC Bonder 75 to a customer, expanding the South Korean equipment maker's reach beyond high-bandwidth memory (HBM) into the broader system semiconductor packaging market. Semiconductor Read
7 DigiTimes Taiwan virtual asset law to help lower supply chain transaction costs Taiwan's Legislative Yuan passed the Virtual Asset Service Act in June 2026, and Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) is now drafting delegated regulations, with completion planned for the first quarter of 2027. PwC Taiwan managing director Monica Lee said banks will need licenses to operate virtual asset se Logistics Read
8 CNA US-China AI race: Rivals compete for influence while seeking common ground on risks Washington and Beijing are competing across AI models, chips and supply chains, even as they explore ways to manage the technology’s growing risks. Southeast Asia is increasingly becoming a focus of their efforts to build international AI partnerships. AISemiconductorLogistics Read
9 CNA MAS warns of fresh global shocks and AI pullback, but says Singapore firms and households well-buffered Economies benefitting from AI-related exports and investments can handle higher debt costs for now, but they are also the most vulnerable if the AI boom cools. AI Read

11 NikkeiAsia Alibaba touts 'most powerful AI chip in China' for data center buildout Alibaba touts 'most powerful AI chip in China' for data center buildout AISemiconductor Read

entry.title: Asia Tech News Digest - September 21, 2026
entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 TechAsia Australian AI firm Firmus plans $5b IPO Firmus has two operating data centers in Australia and Singapore, with five more under development across Asia-Pacific. AI Read
2 CNA UN General Assembly: Wars, geopolitical divides, AI and climate change test global cooperation Nearly 130 heads of state and government are expected in New York for the UN General Assembly’s High-level Week, as multiple global issues test the UN’s ability to find common ground. AI Read
3 DigiTimes Z.ai's ZCode crisis exposes AI coding's enterprise trust gap Chinese AI developer Z.ai has open-sourced its ZCode coding tool and is preparing a zero-data-retention option for its Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) platform after ZCode was found packaging local code repositories and attempting to upload them to the cloud. AI Read
4 DigiTimes TSMC builds Kaohsiung hub to speed advanced packaging tests TSMC is building an advanced packaging validation hub in southern Taiwan as rapid chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) expansion puts pressure on equipment and materials suppliers to qualify new technologies faster. Semiconductor Read
5 DigiTimes Chinese image sensor maker GalaxyCore raises the stakes in high-end CIS GalaxyCore Inc. plans to raise up to CNY4.2 billion (US$627 million) to expand 12-inch CMOS image sensor (CIS) capacity and develop 100MP and 200MP sensors, doubling down on higher-value imaging after its first Fab-Lite investment took longer than expected to deliver returns. Semiconductor Read
6 EETAsia UVJC to Debut NovaJet Dry Thin-Film Deposition System at WESEMiBAY UVJC will showcase NovaJet, a maskless dry deposition system, as semiconductor manufacturing moves toward more flexible processing. The post UVJC to Debut NovaJet Dry Thin-Film Deposition System at WESEMiBAY appeared first on EE Times Asia . Semiconductor Read
7 TechAsia China’s CXMT says new memory-chip platform enters production CXMT used quadruple patterning to shrink memory-cell features to 11.95 nanometres. Semiconductor Read
8 TechAsia Meituan launches AI assistant for hairstylists More than 1.18 million users voted in Meituan’s hairstylist selection. AI Read
